recorded.prompt:q-order:a: Given this page and this question with its key, does a passage of the page rule out this wrong option? Quote the passage.
recorded.outcome:q-order:a: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-order:a: "Case order does not affect performance: `javac` compiles an int switch to a `tableswitch` (direct jump) or a `lookupswitch` (sorted keys, binary search), whatever the order in the source."
recorded.prompt:q-order:b: Given this page and this question with its key, does a passage of the page rule out this wrong option? Quote the passage.
recorded.outcome:q-order:b: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-order:b: "Case order does not affect performance ... whatever the order in the source." excludes even a small effect.
recorded.prompt:q-labels:b: Given this page and this question with its key, does a passage of the page rule out this wrong option? Quote the passage.
recorded.outcome:q-labels:b: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-labels:b: The pitfall "Using non-constant case labels: Case labels must be compile-time constants" excludes values worked out as each case is reached.
recorded.prompt:q-labels:c: Given this page and this question with its key, does a passage of the page rule out this wrong option? Quote the passage.
recorded.outcome:q-labels:c: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-labels:c: The page asks only that "Case labels must be compile-time constants" and its fall-through example uses named enum constants ("case MONDAY: case TUESDAY: ..."), so named constants are not refused.
